head: e1434d6
fail_reasons: security 2 < 7 (critical tier) — SC-4 falsified again by four independent single-write paths, reproduced end-to-end
SC-3 fails: INV-12's '알려진 한계' does not list the path-spelling class, and the body still asserts '_batch_approval 은 단일 쓰기로 교체할 수 없다' — falsified with no rm at all
the rework closed exactly one instance (basename case-variant), not the class the 7th judgment named
issues: [security][critical] SC-4 falsified without any rm: a Write to `<repo>/Progress/Contracts/sprint-54.json` (directory-component case variant, same inode) is ALLOWED and replaces `_batch_approval` with `{scope:["**/*"],N:99}` while `agreed:true` is untouched. `PROGRESS/CONTRACTS/SPRINT-54.JSON` likewise. Verified end-to-end: before=`{scope:[hooks/invariant-guard.sh,tests/invariant-guard.bats],N:3}` → after=`{scope:[**/*],N:99}`.

[security][critical] `canon_file()` does not judge file identity. It normalizes only the LAST path component's spelling; every ancestor component remains an open variant axis. `pwd -P` does not case-normalize directories: bash's `cd` builds PWD by string concatenation and only verifies same-file, so a case-variant directory passes verification and the original spelling survives. Measured: `canon_file '<repo>/Progress/Contracts/SPRINT-54.json'` returns `<repo>/Progress/Contracts/sprint-54.json` — dir spelling unchanged. The commit message 'judge protection by file identity, not by path spelling' (05b2ebf) does not describe what the code does.

[security][critical] `canon_file()` fails OPEN on a missing directory (`d=$(cd "$d") || { printf '%s' "$p"; return 0; }`) — it returns the raw string, which is precisely the delete-then-recreate case. Consequences: `rm <계약>` + one Write to `contracts/SPRINT-54.json` or `contracts/sprint-54.JSON` or `progress/Contracts/sprint-54.json` = ALLOW; `rm -rf progress/contracts` + one Write = ALLOW (the 7th judgment's second reported path, still open).

[security][critical] `canon_file()` is applied at line 291, AFTER three gates that judge on the raw path: the new-file exception (line 198), the awk fail-closed gate (line 210), and the truncation gate (line 263). Ordering defect — the comment at line 277 ('이후의 모든 판정(is_protected·신규생성 예외·계약 브랜치)이 같은 값을 본다') is false for the new-file exception, which runs 93 lines earlier.

[security][critical] INV-7 truncation class reopened by the same axis: an empty Write to `tests/invariant-guard.BATS` is ALLOWED and empties the real file (verified: 1070 → 0 lines). Same for `hooks/INVARIANT-GUARD.SH`, `progress/HARNESS-CONFIG.JSON`, `contracts/SPRINT-54.json`. Canonical spellings correctly DENY, so the gate exists and is simply routed around by spelling.

[security][critical] The class leaks into INV-11, the harness's primary passes gate, and this is worse than anything F68 defends: `rm progress/feature_list.json` (firewall ALLOW) + one Write to `progress/FEATURE_LIST.JSON` sets F68 `passes:true` on a critical-tier feature with no evaluator-feedback lookup, no evaluator-runs check, no min-of-5 and no security-threshold check. Verified end-to-end — after the write, `jq` on `progress/feature_list.json` reports `passes=true`.

[security][high] A file symlink inside the contracts directory (`contracts/alias.json -> sprint-54.json`) is ALLOWED — `canon_file` resolves the directory but never the file, so an alias writes through to the contract. A directory symlink IS resolved (correctly DENY), which shows the asymmetry is in the file leg.

[security][medium] Every prerequisite step is friction-free: `rm progress/feature_list.json`, `rm -rf progress/contracts`, and `rm progress/contracts/sprint-54.json` are all `allow` in pre-bash-firewall.sh. None of these attacks needs an `ask`.

[security][medium] The 7th judgment's secondary finding is unaddressed: `protected-integrity.sh` is still wired only to `PostToolUse: Bash` in both `hooks/hooks.json` and `settings.json`. Every bypass above travels the Write path, so nothing detects or restores them afterward. Neither the contract nor INVARIANTS states this limit.
[error] `canon_file`'s only error branch fails open rather than fail-closed, contradicting the file's own stated principle ('안전장치는 결핍 시 차단이 원칙') applied to jq and awk twelve lines apart.

[error] ES-3 claims two independent layers block an out-of-scope touch ('invariant-guard가 차단(기존) + 배치 루프가 approval-queue.json 적립 후 중단'). Layer 1 demonstrably does not block for the spelling class; layer 2 is loop discipline, not code — so ES-3 has one layer, and it is porous.

[error][low] `canon_file` mangles names containing a newline: `grep -ixF` treats the embedded newline as a pattern separator, so `multi\nline.json` canonicalizes to `.../multi`. Exotic, but it is another fail-open in the same function. Space, glob-meta and leading-dash names are handled correctly (`-F` and `--`).

[test] The rework is pinned by exactly one test. Mutating `FILE=$(canon_file "$FILE")` to a no-op and running the full suite yields 722 ok / 2 not ok — `improve-auto.bats:341 'F68: a case-variant path is the same file'` (which pins the single `SPRINT-93.json` basename instance and skips on case-sensitive filesystems) and an F65 ticket test that reacts incidentally. No test covers directory-case, delete-then-recreate + case variant, symlink alias, truncation via case variant, or the INV-11 leak.
[test][medium] Because the one F68 test `skip`s on case-sensitive filesystems, Linux CI has zero coverage of this entire axis — the guard's behaviour there is asserted by nobody.

[quality] Comments in `invariant-guard.sh` are this repo's design record, and two of them now misstate the code: line 270-278 claims the class is closed 'in one shot' and line 277 claims all downstream judgments see the same value. Both are falsified by the probes above.

[criteria] `progress/contracts/sprint-54.json` carries duplicate JSON keys — `_gap_6th` appears three times and `_downgraded_again` three times inside `security_criteria[3]`. `jq` silently keeps the last, so two-thirds of the recorded judgment history is unreadable through any jq-based tooling. This is an audit-record defect in the very file AC-6 designates as the audit record.

acceptance: AC-1: skills/implement/SKILL.md §9 defines `--auto N` with the three batch-gate items (범위·N·중단조건), the unattended repeat procedure, and a reference to `/improve --auto`; pinned by doc-parsing tests in the green suite
AC-2: skills/change-request/SKILL.md §9 (line 112) replaces the Step 9 per-item confirmation with a single batch Plan gate and chains into `/implement --auto N`
AC-3: fail policy `revert-and-continue` (default) / `queue-and-stop` is documented at implement/SKILL.md:174-175 with the branch behaviour
AC-4: evaluator call protocol is documented at implement/SKILL.md §8.5 and referenced from ADR-006:50

AC-5: five machine-decidable stop conditions at implement/SKILL.md:179-187, each naming the file/value it is decided from (evaluator-feedback score, failed_criteria intersection, approval-queue.json, 900s timeout)
AC-6: `_batch_approval` records scope/N/policy in the Sprint Contract and per-turn verdicts are preserved as individual evaluator-feedback-*.json files (14 present)
security: SC-1 (threshold leg only): progress/harness-config.json shows no threshold change; full suite green at 724/724 — no regression introduced by the rework commits

SC-4 (canonical-path leg only): a Write to the exactly-spelled `progress/contracts/sprint-54.json` replacing `_batch_approval` on an `agreed:true` contract is correctly DENIED, and so is the basename case variant `SPRINT-54.json` that the 7th judgment reported (this is the one instance 05b2ebf closed)
error_scenarios: ES-1: 900s timeout → one retry → `queue-and-stop` is specified at implement/SKILL.md:187
ES-2: repeat-defect stop condition is specified as the intersection of the previous and current `failed_criteria`

security: SC-4: '승인 범위 조작이 단일 쓰기로는 불가능하다' — falsified by four independent single-write paths (dir-case variant with no rm; rm + case-variant basename; rm + case-variant dir; rm -rf of the contracts dir; plus a file-symlink alias)
SC-3: 'INV-12·ADR-006 개정이 약화가 아니라 조건부 확대임을 문서가 정확히 서술한다' — the '알려진 한계' list omits the path-spelling class entirely while the body asserts single-write replacement is impossible
SC-2 (enforcement leg): '승인된 범위 안에서만' cannot hold while the loop can rewrite the scope record in one write
SC-1 (substance leg): the per-turn gates are not unweakened in practice — one write empties a protected test file and one write flips a critical feature's `passes`
error_scenarios: ES-3: the claimed two independent layers are one porous layer; invariant-guard does not block the spelling class

missing_criteria: No criterion requires the guard's protection decision to be made on resolved file identity (device+inode, or realpath) rather than on a path string — this is the axis that has now failed in rounds 6, 7 and 8, and it is nowhere in the contract
No criterion covers the Write path having no post-hoc integrity layer, even though the 7th judgment raised it; protected-integrity.sh remains PostToolUse:Bash only
No criterion requires the F68 tests to be meaningful on case-sensitive filesystems, so CI coverage of this axis is zero
ambiguous_criteria: SC-4's '단일 쓰기' is counted per Write tool call while the `rm` that precedes it is free (firewall allow) — under that accounting a two-step attack reads as 'single write'. The criterion should count operations, not Write calls.
security_criteria_insufficient: SC-4 has been downgraded twice (`_downgraded`, `_downgraded_again`) and its enforcement point re-narrowed each round. It is now narrow enough that satisfying it literally would still leave INV-11 and INV-7 bypassable by the same technique.
criteria_gaps.action_required: Do not open a 9th code round on SC-4 as written. Either implement one identity-based decision (resolve the target to device+inode when it exists, and to realpath(parent)+FS-spelled basename when it does not, applied immediately after FILE is extracted and before every consumer), or descope SC-4 to F69 (the ExitPlanMode-history control the contract already names as the only forgery-proof point). Independently of that choice, the INV-11 and INV-7 leaks below are pre-existing guard defects, not F68 scope, and must be fixed regardless.

convergence_assessment.verdict: not converging on the current strategy
convergence_assessment.evidence: Probing the pre-rework guard (d682e3a) against the same four cases shows the rework changed exactly one outcome: basename case-variant ALLOW→DENY. Directory-case scope replacement, the INV-11 recreate leak, and the truncation leak are byte-identical before and after. Rounds 6, 7 and 8 each closed the single instance the previous judgment happened to demonstrate.
convergence_assessment.recommendation: Descope. Ship F68 on AC-1..AC-6 + SC-1..SC-3 with INV-12 honestly recording that the write-path spelling class is open, and move SC-4 to F69 where the forgery-proof control lives. Raise the INV-11/INV-7 spelling leaks as their own critical item — leaving `rm feature_list.json` + one Write → `passes:true` open is a larger exposure than the scope-widening SC-4 was written to prevent.
convergence_assessment.stop_condition_triggered: ES-2 / stop condition 3 (같은 결함 반복): the failed_criteria intersection with the 7th judgment is SC-4 on the identical axis, for the third consecutive round.

evidence.environment: macOS APFS, case-insensitive (verified: touch .casetest → ls .CASETEST succeeds). Probes run against a git clone of HEAD e1434d6 at $SCRATCH/repo with a `_batch_approval` seeded and committed, so the HEAD-comparison leg of the guard is live. The real repository was not modified.
evidence.regression_suite: bats tests/ (no pipe, redirected to $SCRATCH/bats.out): plan `1..724`, `^ok` = 724, `^not ok` = 0, exit 0. Corpus size 724 ≥ 700.
evidence.guard_probes_contract_scope: Write of `_batch_approval={scope:["**/*"],N:99}` into the agreed contract, by spelling: canonical DENY | `SPRINT-54.json` DENY | `sprint-54.JSON` DENY | `Progress/Contracts/sprint-54.json` **ALLOW** | `PROGRESS/CONTRACTS/SPRINT-54.JSON` **ALLOW** | `./x//y` DENY | `..` traversal DENY | dir-symlink DENY | file-symlink alias **ALLOW** | relative path DENY
evidence.guard_probes_delete_then_recreate: after removing the contract: canonical DENY | `SPRINT-54.json` **ALLOW** | `sprint-54.JSON` **ALLOW** | `progress/Contracts/sprint-54.json` **ALLOW**. After `rm -rf progress/contracts`: **ALLOW**.
evidence.end_to_end_scope_replacement: cp evil.json '<repo>/PROGRESS/CONTRACTS/SPRINT-54.JSON' → jq on progress/contracts/sprint-54.json reports `_batch_approval` = {"scope":["**/*"],"N":99,...}, `agreed` still true. Restored via git checkout.
evidence.guard_probes_truncation: empty Write: `tests/invariant-guard.bats` DENY | `tests/invariant-guard.BATS` **ALLOW** | `hooks/invariant-guard.sh` DENY | `hooks/INVARIANT-GUARD.SH` **ALLOW** | `progress/harness-config.json` DENY | `progress/HARNESS-CONFIG.JSON` **ALLOW** | `contracts/SPRINT-54.json` **ALLOW** | `Hooks/invariant-guard.sh` DENY. End-to-end: `: > tests/invariant-guard.BATS` took the real file from 1070 to 0 lines.
evidence.inv11_leak: feature_list.json with F68 passes:true — canonical DENY | `FEATURE_LIST.JSON` (file present) DENY | `Progress/feature_list.json` DENY | delete-then-recreate canonical DENY | delete-then-recreate `FEATURE_LIST.JSON` **ALLOW**. End-to-end: after `rm progress/feature_list.json` + write, `jq '.features[]|select(.id=="F68")|.passes'` on progress/feature_list.json = true.
evidence.firewall_reachability: pre-bash-firewall.sh decisions: `rm progress/feature_list.json` → allow; `rm -rf progress/contracts` → allow; `rm progress/contracts/sprint-54.json` → allow.
evidence.canon_file_characterization: isolated function: `Progress/Contracts/SPRINT-54.json` → `Progress/Contracts/sprint-54.json` (dir spelling preserved); missing directory → raw path returned unchanged (fail-open); `A B.json`, `A*B.json`, `-N.json` → correct (thanks to `-F`/`--`); embedded newline → truncated to first line.
evidence.before_after_attribution: Same four probes against `git show d682e3a:hooks/invariant-guard.sh` (pre-rework): truncation leak ALLOW→ALLOW, INV-11 leak ALLOW→ALLOW, dir-case scope replace ALLOW→ALLOW, basename-case ALLOW→DENY. The rework changed exactly one outcome.
evidence.test_teeth: MUT-1: `FILE=$(canon_file "$FILE")` replaced with a no-op, full suite re-run in the clone → plan 1..724, ok 722, not ok 2 — `F68: a case-variant path is the same file (F37 7차 판정)` and `F65: 티켓은 내용에 묶이고 정착할 때 소비된다`. The rework is pinned by one instance-level test that skips on case-sensitive filesystems.
evidence.hook_trace: bash -x of the guard on the dir-case payload shows `FILE=.../repo/Progress/Contracts/sprint-54.json` after canon_file, then `[[ ... == */contracts/* ]]` failing and the script reaching the terminal `exit 0` without entering the contract branch.
evidence.f67_scope_note: hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh, tests/pre-bash-firewall.bats and the F67 paragraphs of INV-14 were not evaluated (separate judgment). The firewall was consulted read-only, to establish reachability of the `rm` steps above; no F68 defect reproduced inside F67's changes.
